Desert Globe

30 mapped deserts

A desert is defined principally by dryness — not heat or sand. Many receive under about 250 mm / 10 in of precipitation a year, though evaporation and seasonal water availability matter too.

Approximate extents — boundaries are definition-dependent

Select a desert on the globe or from the list. Every figure carries its own qualification: areas vary with the boundary used, ages describe the history of dry conditions rather than the rock beneath, and where a source could not be verified the field says so rather than guessing.
All 30 deserts
Land geometry: Natural Earth 1:50m via world-atlas. Desert extents and species ranges are approximate outlines drawn for orientation, not survey data.

A field identification walk

Desert Field Walk

Three deserts, built to their real ground: the Kalahari's red vegetated dunes, the Atacama's salt-and-gravel pampa under the driest sky on Earth, and the Chihuahuan limestone basin. Walk until you find something living, then name it. Every plant and animal is modelled from the features a field guide would actually use — the gemsbok's straight horns, the shepherd's tree's white trunk, the kit fox's outsized ears.

Click the ground to walk there. Click anything — plant, animal, track or outcrop — to go and examine it. Drag to look around. B raises binoculars for distant movement.
Animals leave their real spoor: cut a trail, read the print, take the bearing it gives you and follow.
Prefer keys? WS walk, AD turn, Shift to run, E to examine, N for the notebook, Esc to stop. The ◎ button turns on mouse-look if you want it.
AD or ←→ swing the view a full 360° · Q turns you around · R lets it drift round on its own · ? beside the notebook shows every control.
On a touchscreen: the left pad walks and steers, drag elsewhere to look, or just tap what you see.

How to move and look

Controls

Click the ground
Walk to that spot
Click a plant, animal, track or outcrop
Walk over and examine it
Drag
Look around
WS / ↑↓
Walk forward and back
AD / ←→
Turn the view — hold to swing a full 360°
Shift
Run, and turn faster
Q or ⟲
Turn around, 180°
R or ↻
Slow 360° survey — eases in, drifts round, eases out
B or ⌖
Binoculars; narrows the view and steadies the aim
E
Examine whatever is in front of you
N or ☰
Field notebook
◎
Mouse-look, if you prefer it to dragging
Esc
Stop walking, close a card
